name: parking
description: A multi-level car park: spaces, tickets, hourly rates with a daily cap, monthly permits, an SQLite ticket log and revenue reports.
author: harness developer (dev split)

issues.description: Every started hour should be billed in full, but the minutes are rounded to the nearest hour, so 61 minutes bill as one hour and 2 h 10 min as two.
issues.fix_hint: Round up: any minutes past a whole hour start another billable hour.

issues.description: The daily cap should apply to each 24 hours of a stay, but it caps the whole stay, so a three-day stay costs the same as one day.
issues.fix_hint: Charge daily_cap for each full 24 hours and the capped hourly price for the remaining hours.

issues.description: The docstring promises the days with the most revenue, highest first, but the sort is ascending, so it returns the quietest days.
issues.fix_hint: Sort by revenue in descending order (reverse=True) before taking the first count.

issues.description: The plate is pasted into the SQL text, so a plate such as x' OR '1'='1 returns every ticket in the log (and a quote in a plate breaks the query).
issues.fix_hint: Use a ? placeholder and pass the plate as a query parameter.

issues.description: The pricing module, which the desk and the reports build on, imports the revenue report module (and through it the SQLite storage and the permit registry) just to round money; the rounding helper belongs in a low-level module.
The 20% VAT rate is written as a bare 1.2 in two functions in two modules instead of one named constant.

issues.anchor: def revenue_report(tickets: list[Ticket], permits: list[Permit], year: int, month: int) -> str:
issues.description: One 50-line function filters the month, totals per day and per level, computes stay statistics, sums permits and formats every section; each section could be its own function.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: The column name is formatted into the SQL, but only after it is checked against a fixed list of column names; values that are not on the list are refused.
The -1 and +1 convert between 1-based months and a 0-based month index, so year rollover is right, and the day is clamped to the length of the target month.
